known_vulnerabilities.description: The centralized sequencer can selectively exclude transactions, enabling MEV extraction, front-running, and denial-of-service against specific addresses; currently no cryptographic enforcement of inclusion

known_vulnerabilities.title: Forced Inclusion Delay Exploitation
known_vulnerabilities.description: L1 forced inclusion (delayed inbox) has a mandatory delay window (24h on Arbitrum); attackers can exploit the delay to perform L1 actions that affect L2 state after the forced transaction is known but before it is included

known_vulnerabilities.title: State Root Challenge Period Attacks
known_vulnerabilities.description: During the 7-day (Optimism) or variable (Arbitrum) challenge period, the state root is provisional; protocols that finalize L2→L1 messages before the challenge period expires are vulnerable to state root fraud proofs reverting assumed-final transactions

known_vulnerabilities.title: Gas Price Oracle Manipulation
known_vulnerabilities.description: L2 gas price oracles derive from L1 base fee and L2 congestion; during L1 fee spikes the gas oracle may be temporarily manipulated, causing mispriced transactions and MEV opportunities for sequencer-adjacent actors
